statusDetail: All 58 catalog checks were judged. Product-detail and unknown-route failures were recorded as observed site issues rather than hidden as untested work. Account, basket and payment submission were not attempted because product detail failed before those states and no purchase was authorized.

page.notes: Large German commerce MPA/hybrid. Representative coverage includes homepage, category, search, two product-detail attempts and an error route. Not covered: authenticated account, basket/payment submission, post-purchase, or additional category templates; those require credentials/transaction authority or were downstream of the reproducible product-page failure.

paths.description: Homepage and global navigation, consent, promotions and recommendations; represents the shared shell and landing template.
Sofas category listing; represents taxonomy navigation, filters and product-grid discovery.
Search results for “sofa”; represents search, filter and product discovery on mobile.
Representative product-detail navigation from the category. Two products were attempted; both rendered an empty page under the audited browser after anti-bot HTTP 429 signals.
Synthetic unknown route; represents the HTTP 404 recovery state.

findings.summary: The site does not provide a usable preference-driven dark theme.
findings.evidence: Light and dark screenshots are pixel-identical in the first viewport, while the platform probe found only limited color-scheme-related CSS in the readable sheets.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare supported color schemes and retint surfaces, text, controls and imagery under prefers-color-scheme; verify contrast in both themes.

findings.summary: Loading animation continues when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe found fourteen running 800 ms animations and no readable prefers-reduced-motion rules; the active elements were rotating loading spinners.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce treatment that removes non-essential rotation and uses a static progress affordance where continuous motion is unnecessary.

findings.summary: The first-visit consent dialog dominates and blocks the primary content on desktop and mobile.
findings.evidence: Screenshots of home, category and mobile search show the dialog covering most of the content; on 360x800 it consumes nearly the entire viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the least intrusive consent presentation legally possible, keep equal accept/reject controls immediately visible, and avoid obscuring unrelated content.

findings.summary: Several global navigation targets are only 24 px high.
findings.evidence: The focus/target probe measured category navigation buttons such as “Mode”, “Sport” and “Sale” at 24 px high, below comfortable touch-target guidance.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase the interactive hit area to at least 44 CSS px without necessarily increasing the visual glyph size, and verify visible :focus-visible styling.

findings.summary: The representative product journey dead-ends on a blank product page in the audited client.
findings.evidence: Two product links discovered from category/search were opened in fresh browser sessions; both screenshots are blank and the first product DOM has no title, H1, text or controls. HAR/Lighthouse also recorded an anti-bot 429.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a recoverable challenge or server-rendered product fallback instead of a blank response, and ensure legitimate browsers/agents can reach product detail and continue shopping.

findings.summary: Unknown routes return a bare 404 with no recovery path.
findings.evidence: The same-origin unknown-route probe returned status 404 and only “404 Not Found”, with no home, search, retry or back affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a branded 404 state that explains what happened and offers search, home, back and help actions while preserving the original context.

findings.summary: Mobile load performance is far outside the good Core Web Vitals range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 21.6 s, TBT 620 ms and CLS 0.126 (performance 38). The independent trace measured LCP 4.92 s and seven long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP dependency chain, prioritize the true LCP asset, reduce initial JavaScript and CSS, and split/defer non-critical work.

findings.summary: Late content causes measurable layout shift.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured CLS 0.126 and the mobile layout observer independently recorded a 0.063 shift near 5 seconds; 27 images lacked explicit dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve dimensions/aspect-ratio for images and late modules, and make font fallbacks metrically compatible.

findings.summary: Heavy scripting blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded seven long tasks, the longest 228 ms, with 212 ms TBT; Lighthouse measured 620 ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Break work into yieldable tasks, prioritize interaction work, and defer recommendation, account and consent code until needed.

findings.summary: The entry page has an excessive request and render-blocking footprint.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 631 requests and 3.23 MB transferred, including 343 scripts, 28 stylesheets and numerous parser-inserted high-priority stylesheets; Lighthouse LCP was 21.6 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, defer non-critical component bundles, preload only the confirmed LCP resource and preserve long-lived cacheability.

findings.summary: Substantial unused JavaScript and CSS ship on initial load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 164 KiB unused JavaScript and 82 KiB unused CSS, including 57% of the 130 KiB consent SDK and 85–90% of two global/component stylesheets.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by visible feature, remove legacy/global CSS from the initial route and load consent/account/recommendation modules conditionally.

findings.summary: Important images, links, commands and the search field lack accessible names or visible labels.
findings.evidence: axe reported 14 image-alt failures, three unnamed links, two unnamed ARIA commands and a title-only search label; the image primitive counted 28 images without alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Add meaningful alt text, accessible names and visible labels; use empty alt only for genuinely decorative images and native semantics where possible.

findings.summary: Product and energy-label text fails minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: axe found 18 serious color-contrast failures in recommendation prices and energy-label links; Lighthouse also failed color-contrast.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background design tokens to meet WCAG AA in every state and theme, then retest rendered cards with axe.

findings.summary: Landmark structure is repetitive and much content sits outside landmarks.
findings.evidence: axe found duplicate/non-unique banner landmarks and 162 region violations; the probe also found programmatically focused global controls with no computed outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one banner landmark, uniquely label repeated landmarks, place major content in main/section landmarks and implement an obvious :focus-visible indicator.

findings.summary: The page logs runtime and network errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a 429 resource failure and an aborted Summarizer API request caused by unsupported language configuration.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle anti-bot/network responses without console errors and validate Summarizer language capabilities before creating a session.

findings.summary: Numerous images have missing dimensions or distorted aspect ratios.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 27 images without width/height and 19 oversized images; Lighthouse listed multiple product images displayed at 136×187 despite 350×500 source proportions.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio, preserve object-fit intentionally, and serve responsive sources matched to display size.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs, missing source maps and BFCache blockers reduce platform hygiene.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported three deprecated API warnings, missing source maps for large first-party bundles and three BFCache failure reasons including cache-control:no-store.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated storage/ad-tech API usage, publish valid source maps to controlled access, and scope no-store headers so eligible pages can use BFCache.

findings.summary: Some controls presented as links are not crawlable or descriptively named.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors and link-text; homepage recon found “Mein Konto” uses javascript:void(0), while axe found unnamed links.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href URLs for navigation, reserve buttons for actions, and give every link descriptive accessible text.

findings.summary: The homepage lacks complete social preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The metadata probe found JSON-LD but no og:title value; title, description and canonical were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph and equivalent share metadata aligned with the visible page and retain valid Organization/WebSite JSON-LD.

findings.summary: Several first-party cookies are sent without Secure or with broad SameSite=None posture.
findings.evidence: Cookie audit found six cookies; OptanonConsent and KP_UIDz lacked Secure, and five used SameSite=None. HTTPS, HSTS, CSP frame-ancestors and nosniff were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark every HTTPS cookie Secure, use Lax/Strict unless cross-site delivery is required, and review identifiers for minimum lifetime and scope.

findings.summary: Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are absent.
findings.evidence: Header audit found HSTS, CSP frame-ancestors and nosniff, but no Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a restrictive Referrer-Policy and a feature-specific Permissions-Policy; keep frame-ancestors as the clickjacking control.

findings.summary: HTTP failures degrade to blank or bare responses.
findings.evidence: Product navigation produced blank documents alongside HTTP 429 evidence, while an unknown route returned only bare “404 Not Found” with no recovery controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Render resilient, accessible error states for 404, 429, timeout and offline conditions with retry, search and safe navigation actions.

findings.summary: The global search input is unlabeled and disables browser autocomplete.
findings.evidence: DOM probe found the only homepage text input has autocomplete="off", no associated label and no aria-label; axe flagged it as title-only.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a visible label or robust accessible name and avoid disabling autocomplete unless the custom suggestions demonstrably provide a better, accessible equivalent.

findings.summary: The commercial flow cannot reach a product detail in the audited client.
findings.evidence: Two visible, descriptive product links from listing pages led to blank pages, preventing inspection of pricing commitment, basket, checkout, cancellation and reauthentication states.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace silent anti-bot failure with a proportionate recoverable verification state and preserve product/pricing context through the challenge.

findings.summary: Image delivery is not consistently resolution- and viewport-efficient.
findings.evidence: Image audit found 19 oversized images, 27 without responsive srcset and 66 below-fold images not lazy-loaded; the page transferred 994 KB of images.
findings.suggestedFix: Use responsive srcset/sizes or the image CDN’s equivalent, lazy-load genuinely below-fold media and preserve eager/fetchpriority only for the LCP image.

findings.summary: The initial route ships a disproportionate script and subdomain footprint.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 343 script requests and 1.64 MB script transfer; 479 cross-origin requests moved 2.38 MB, mostly OTTO static/image subdomains, plus a 130 KB consent SDK.
findings.suggestedFix: Set route-level request/byte budgets, collapse component fragmentation, defer non-essential scripts and audit every consent/recommendation dependency for user value.

findings.summary: The commerce surface exposes no structured agent tools.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM/source inspection found no WebMCP or agentic-tool registration even though robots.txt explicitly permits major AI user agents and the site exposes purchasable products.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose narrowly scoped, confirmable product search, detail, basket and order-status capabilities via WebMCP/agentic forms with explicit user control.

findings.summary: The page calls the Summarizer API with unsupported language configuration.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse console evidence says the Summarizer API request was aborted because unsupported languages were specified and lists the supported language codes.
findings.suggestedFix: Feature-detect the Summarizer API, query capability/language support and only create sessions with supported input/output languages; provide a graceful fallback.

findings.summary: The homepage has a very large baseline memory footprint.
findings.evidence: Heap summaries measured 80.8–85.5 MB self size with 1.42–1.51 million V8 nodes; the post snapshot contained over 203k closures. This is high for a landing page even allowing for commerce complexity.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce initial component/script population, unload closed surfaces and lazy-initialize recommendation/account/consent features.

taskList.title: Cut the initial network/main-thread footprint and fix LCP
Restore a recoverable product and HTTP-error journey
Fix names, alternatives, labels, landmarks, focus and contrast
Make consent content-first without weakening choice
Harden cookies and defensive response policies
Clean console, deprecated APIs, source maps and BFCache blockers
Repair crawlable links and social metadata
Validate built-in AI languages and expose safe agent tools
